author: node-limit-audit
body:
Independent audit of integrated runtime changes: no actionable correctness issue found in the reviewed scope.

- API validation is strict (type(value) is int, 1..1,048,576), and occurs before repository resolution. CLI defaults to 131,072 and passes the parsed value through the API.
- Both Lean helper profiles receive the same numeric allowance. The generated Lean command interpolates only the validated integer; both traversal functions retain original traversal behavior and enforce node/depth limits.
- Both correspondence replay paths pass stored limits.nodes; validation checks the stored node budget, and implementation digest includes the new limits module. The current helper command syntax has no other repository callers.
- No traversal cache was retained in the production diff. Evidence shows 109,620 vs 10,711 traversal visits and 0.098s vs 0.025s traversal medians, while end-to-end process medians are 1.448s vs 1.390s and peak RSS is effectively unchanged (~3.82 GB). This supports deferring the cache; it does not establish full extraction success.
- Actual default-budget evidence records complete:false/status:unavailable due to Unknown identifier inst in the printed-context roundtrip, so no full-slice success claim is present.
- Compared node-budget-tests-before-refactor.py against tests/test_proof_slice_limits.py: the 10 assertion expressions across 12 parameterized cases are preserved; valid-shape assertions were factored into a helper without removing checks. The replay test still asserts supported status and both 37,000-node replay calls.
- Scope audit: runtime changes are limited to the named proof slice/correspondence modules, Lean helpers, and new focused tests; current unrelated dirty docs/OpenSpec/skill files remain present and were not edited by this audit. No tests/builds/executions were run.

Reviewed diff was read-only.
